comments.text:
ambient temps matter...
Temperature at OLED layer
~20–30°C Ideal operating range; slow degradation
~30–40°C Normal for many monitors; some acceleration
~40–50°C Noticeably faster aging, especially at high brightness
~50–60°C+ Significantly increased degradation risk
Gaming/high brightness puts the Oled at 10-20c over ambient.
So if you live in a climate thats 30-40c part of the year, and gaming the OLED is going to burn in far faster then a 18c aircon controlled 24h room.

OLEDs are most definitely sturdier than people realise. It’s just a loud minority of people with the problem. As per usual, most people who don’t have issues don’t come forward and say so, so you only hear of the 1% that do have issues.

TN, IPS and VA all have horrible downsides, some have issues which are apparent and quite intrusive from the minute you first get them. For example, the fact that TN is so washed out it’s basically greyscale by today’s standard, IPS has backlight bleed in every unit though it varies as to how much, and VAs are just really slow. Also Mini-LED blooming is far more noticeable than burn-in.

I just find it extremely odd that people bash OLEDs for their burn-in issue when it’s actually less distracting and annoying than the common issues of the other display types.
